record.entity_title: Swiss tax residency and worldwide income (EU/EFTA)
record.fact_text: If you become tax-resident in Switzerland — by settling with intent to stay, or by staying at least 30 days while working (or 90 days without working) — you have unlimited Swiss tax liability on your worldwide income, except for foreign businesses, permanent establishments and real estate.
record.evidence_quote: Bei persönlicher Zugehörigkeit ist die Steuerpflicht unbeschränkt; sie erstreckt sich aber nicht auf Geschäftsbetriebe, Betriebsstätten und Grundstücke im Ausland.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: Switzerland uses a 183-day rule and only taxes your Swiss salary. Actually: Swiss domestic law triggers tax residence after a 30-day stay with gainful activity (or 90 days without), and residents are taxed on worldwide income. Action required: check the applicable double-taxation treaty and your move date.

record.entity_title: EU citizen municipal registration (iscrizione anagrafica) after 3 months
record.fact_text: As an EU citizen staying in Italy for more than three months you must obtain iscrizione anagrafica (registration in the resident-population registry) at your comune; registration is required once three months from entry have passed, and an attestation is issued immediately.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: an EU citizen has nothing to file in Italy. Actually: staying beyond three months creates a duty to obtain iscrizione anagrafica at your comune, and the attestation is needed for many later procedures. Action required: register at the Milan comune once you have an address.
